## Overview

The Apache Kafka project released version 4.4.0 on October 22, 2026, and the bugfix release 4.3.2 on October 23, 2026, according to its [downloads page](https://kafka.apache.org/community/downloads/). editor_notes.content_quality: News piece, 711 words (range 400-1200). Clear structure: overview, 4.4.0 features, deprecations, 4.3.2 fixes, and an explicit 'What the Sources Do Not Say' section. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference. Single-vendor sourcing is disclosed and no independent testing is claimed.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots source-0/1/2.html.gz read from disk (sha256 of decompressed content matches manifest; suspicious_patterns null for all three). Live re-fetch via raw curl of all three URLs produced byte-identical sha256 hashes to the snapshots. source-0 (4.4.0 announcement, by Omnia Ibrahim, Oct 22 2026): confirms '25 KIPs and 963 commits since 4.3.0'; KIP-1191 'Dead-letter queues for share groups' with the exact quoted sentence about records 'released beyond the max delivery count, or rejected by the share consumer, become eligible for the DLQ once the share.version feature is upgraded to 2' and the errors.deadletterqueue.* settings; KIP-1241 remote.copy.lag.bytes/ms with the quoted 'allowing tiered storage redundancy to be reduced with delayed upload'; KIP-1312 kafka-cluster.sh unregister-controller and metadata version 4.4-IV2; KIP-909 bootstrap.resolve.timeout.ms default 0 'preserves the historical synchronous behavior', Streams and Connect not yet supported; KIP-892 transactional state stores, enable.transactional.statestores default false, 'only writes since the last successful commit are lost and replayed'; KIP-1357 and KIP-1331 as described; KIP-1209 internal.topics.automatic.creation.enable default true, 'fails at startup if any are missing'; deprecations KIP-1232 (broker.id, no replacement or timeline stated in the announcement, and the article states none), KIP-1200 (removal in Kafka 5.0), KIP-1301, and kafka-broker-api-versions.sh deprecated, to be removed in the next major release, replacement kafka-cluster.sh api-versions (KIP-1220); KIP-1170 quote verbatim; '151 contributors (and 8 AIs)' verbatim. source-1 (4.3.2 announcement, by Ken Huang, Oct 23 2026): 'a bugfix release that fixes around 60 issues since the 4.3.1 release, most notably two potential data loss issues in tiered storage size-based retention and time index truncation' verbatim; KAFKA-20732 and KAFKA-20979 descriptions verbatim; the announcement itself says 'data loss' (so the headline 'data-loss bugs' is supported, and the summary's 'potential' matches the source wording); Streams fixes (KAFKA-20808/20827/20721/20805) and 'published CVEs in jackson-databind, lz4-java, log4j and Jetty' confirmed. source-2 (downloads page): 4.4.0 released Oct 22 2026, 4.3.2 released Oct 23 2026; Supported releases list is exactly 4.4.0, 4.3.2, 4.2.2 (older ones under Archived Releases). All dates match. All three sources are the project's own; independent sources: 0 (News, not Analysis). kafka.apache.org is on config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment. The pattern scanner produced no hits (suspicious_patterns null for all three).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, KIP/KAFKA id, config name, date and quote traced to the sources; no discrepancies. The internal link /article/2026-10/31-apache-kafkas-cve-list-... resolves to an existing published article (file present) and is described accurately; the article does not tie the releases to the CVEs, consistent with the earlier piece (which said the announcements do not name the 12 entries). Minor editorial inference: 'One change affects rollbacks and tooling' for KIP-1170 is a mild characterisation of forward-incompatibility, supported by the quoted text. The title (163 chars) exceeds the 150-char recommendation flagged by chief:review; stylistic only, not an accuracy issue.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, attributed to the announcements throughout.
